planning_assumptions: PRD says 'Change title to anything' — developer will pick a new creative title to replace 'Crunchy Number Muncher'.

tasks.title: Change app title to a new name
tasks.description:
1. WHAT: Change the app title from 'Crunchy Number Muncher' to any new creative title of your choosing across all files and tests.
2. READ FIRST: Read index.html, src/App.tsx, and src/App.test.tsx to see all occurrences of the current title 'Crunchy Number Muncher'.
3. FILES: Modify index.html (line 7, <title> tag), src/App.tsx (line 55, <h1> tag), and src/App.test.tsx (all occurrences of 'Crunchy Number Muncher' in test assertions — lines 24, 29, 39, 44, 67, 80, 99, 119).
4. APPROACH: Do a simple string replacement of 'Crunchy Number Muncher' with the new title in all three files. Make sure every occurrence is updated so tests still pass. No new files needed.
5. PATTERNS: This is a straightforward find-and-replace. The test file uses the title string in queryByText, getByText, and closest calls — all must match the new title exactly.
acceptance_criteria: The page heading after login displays the new title instead of 'Crunchy Number Muncher'
The browser tab title shows the new name instead of 'Crunchy Number Muncher'

tasks.title: Validate title change and run test suite
tasks.description:
1. WHAT: Run the full Vitest test suite to confirm the title rename did not break any tests.
2. READ FIRST: Read package.json to confirm the test command.
3. FILES: Run tests against src/App.test.tsx and all other test files.
4. APPROACH: Run npx vitest run to execute the full test suite. All tests should pass with the new title.
5. PATTERNS: Previous QA tasks ran npx vitest run from the project root.
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run exits with code 0 — all tests pass
npx tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 — no type errors
